idea.title: Goodbye was a blessing
idea.summary: Goodbye began as the blessing God be with ye, squashed into one word in the 1500s; closes on every stranger's bye being a small well-wish.
hookOptions: Goodbye used to be a prayer
Goodbye has God hiding inside it
You say a blessing every time you hang up
Goodbye is a prayer in disguise
sources: Etymonline: goodbye, 1570s, contraction of God be with ye, with good altered by good day, good night
Merriam-Webster: goodbye is a contraction of God be with you
Uncertain part: the influence of good day and good night is described as likely, not certain

scenes.say: You say goodbye every day. It began as a prayer.
People used to part by saying, God be with ye.
By the 1570s, people had mashed it into one word: goodbye.
Dictionaries think good crept in from good day and good night.

scenes.name: Humble Falcon
scenes.label: Call ending
scenes.say: So when a stranger says bye, it's a tiny well-wish. Still.
Next time you say bye, mean it.
